evidence: paper: (U_0, E_0)(X, \eta) = \begin{cases} (U_{\mathrm{in}}, E_{\mathrm{in}})(X, \eta), & X \le X_h, \\ (U_{\mathrm{out}}, E_{\mathrm{out}})(X, \eta), & X \ge X_h. \end{cases}

provenance.note: machine audit: worker, gate, reviewer; not confirmed by a human

verdicts.summary: Lean has an equivalent formula. Same piecewise definition, written in the rescaled radius. The paper puts X_h = X_R e^{-5} and cuts at X ≤ X_h; Lean works with x = X / X_R and cuts at p.1 ≤ matchFraction = Real.exp (-5), the two cuts being the same set under x = X/X_R (matchRadius, line 144, records X_h = matchingRadius * matchFraction in unrescaled form). That the Lean radius variable is the rescaled one was checked against idealE (line 176), which is idealAmplitude * p.1^(1/10) with OutgoingSchedule.shape η = (1+η^2)⁻¹, matching the paper's common value (4η, P_*(1+η^2)^{-1}(X/X_R)^{1/10}) on the overlap. One encoding choice: the paper's two branches overlap at X = X_h (the clauses read X ≤ X_h and X ≥ X_h, consistent because, in the paper's words, both definitions agree 'on a neighborhood of X_h'); Lean's if-then-else is a total function and assigns the single point x = e^{-5} to the inner branch. Recovery is the paper's own overlap statement.
